obtained.how: the publisher's open-access PDF (CC BY; 'Open access funding provided by Fisheries & Oceans Canada'). Springer's PDF link answers first with a 303 to its anonymous cookie handshake (idp.springer.com/authorize?response_type=cookie — no login), which getsrc does not follow; curl with the same honest user agent followed it and saved the PDF, then getsrc --file indexed it

bibliography.checked_against: the article's first page (Environ Biol Fish (2024) 107:1529–1545) and Crossref
bibliography.note: issue 12 is from Crossref; published online 16 August 2024

claims.claim: white suckers in Turkey Lake, Ontario selected 10–16 °C
claims.location: p. 1529 (PDF p. 1), Abstract; p. 1536 (PDF p. 8), Results, Fig. 3
claims.quote: a strong temperature selection preference for thermal habitat between 10 and 16 °C
claims.conditions: pooled over the open-water seasons (spring, summer, fall); by season: spring 12–16 °C, summer only 14–16 °C, fall 10–14 °C; no thermal preference in winter; avoided < 6 °C in summer; nine acoustically tagged adults (610–1,700 g) in a 52-ha, 34-m-deep stratified Boreal Shield lake, Dec 2021–Dec 2022 (n = 9 winter, 6 spring, 5 summer and fall)
claims.note: the Discussion (p. 1539) gives a wider 'temperature preference range [10.0, 18.0°C]' for the open-water season

claims.claim: they spent 84–88 % of their time within 1 m of the bottom
claims.quote: within 1 m of the lake bottom with a high affinity to benthic habitat
claims.conditions: share of telemetry positions within 1 m of the bottom in winter, summer and fall (84.4–87.8 %); spring 73.0 %
claims.note: 'of their time' = of their telemetry positions; add 'except in spring (73 %)'

claims.claim: not selecting water above 18 °C in a lake whose surface reached 24.6 °C
claims.location: p. 1539 (PDF p. 11), Discussion; p. 1536 (PDF p. 8), Results
claims.quote: maximum of 24.6 °C; however, warm waters (> 18 °C) were not preferentially selected
claims.conditions: 'Summer water temperatures in Turkey Lake reached a maximum of 24.6 °C' (the lake's temperature string; the paper says 'surface'); Results: 'no preference for warmer habitats (18.0 – 22.0°C)'

claims.claim: white suckers in Turkey Lake wintered about 1.2 m deeper than in summer, with no thermal selection
claims.quote: white suckers were at their deepest in the winter (mean: 6.10 m)
claims.conditions: mean depths: winter 6.10 m; spring 3.78, summer 4.85, fall 4.95 m; winter and fall depths did not differ significantly; winter selection index ŵ = 1 (no thermal preference)
claims.note: 6.10 − 4.85 = 1.25 m (project arithmetic, right); against fall the difference is 1.15 m and not significant

claims.claim: white suckers in Turkey Lake used 14.6–18.4-ha ranges
claims.source_value: these are POOLED, species-level seasonal 95 % kernel utilization distributions of all tagged fish (n = 5–9) in a 52-ha lake, not individual home ranges: 14.6–18.8 ha in Table 2 (the text says 18.4 for spring; Table 2 says 18.8); individuals used 'a small portion of the total area' (individual–group core overlap 0.12–0.22); core areas (50 % KUD) 2.0–4.0 ha
claims.location: p. 1534 (PDF p. 6), Methods; p. 1537 (PDF p. 9), Results; p. 1538 (PDF p. 10), Table 2
claims.quote: We calculated the home range and core area at the species level for each season
claims.note: the sentence sets them beside individual smallmouth home ranges (Opeongo) and bullhead ranges; say 'the tagged fish together used 15–19 ha of a 52-ha lake each season', or drop the comparison

claims.quote: movement rates ranged from 2.10 km/day to 3.16 km/day
claims.conditions: seasonal means of daily horizontal movement; overall mean ± SD 2.6 ± 0.5 km/day; highest in spring and summer
claims.note: the text's 2.10–3.16 differs from Table 2's seasonal means (winter 1,859.7, spring 3,070.7, summer 2,801.3, fall 2,106.3 m/day, i.e. 1.9–3.1 km/d); the source is internally inconsistent — '≈ 2–3 km a day' covers both

notes: One correction: the 14.6–18.4 ha are pooled seasonal ranges of all tagged fish, not individual home ranges (and Table 2 says 18.8). Other useful values: fish generally in the upper 10 m and over bottom < 10 m deep (home ranges 92–96 % habitat ≤ 10 m); in summer mean depth tracked the cool end (~14 °C) of the 14.1–21.2 °C 'optimal' range of Cincotta & Stauffer (1984); seasonal home ranges overlapped 0.74–0.82; vertical movement 25.0 m/day in winter vs a median 41.8 m/day in other seasons; the authors suggest habitat choice may be set by benthic food rather than temperature.
